page: Microsoft Azure E20_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 20 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 10 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include AVX-512 vector extensions with Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), AES cryptographic acceleration, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 160 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-heavy operations. The instance does not include discrete GPUs or bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced multi-threaded throughput alongside modest single-core execution speed. Single-core stress-ng execution registers in the lower quartile, mirrored by single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates. When all 20 vCPUs are engaged, throughput scales to expected enterprise levels, achieving 18,613.51 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 8,313.0 in Geekbench multi-core evaluation. Memory subsystem testing reflects 88.48 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 43.27 GB/sec in large-block writes, supporting 16.52 million Redis SET operations per second.

Cost efficiency is tied directly to the high memory-to-vCPU allocation. For organizations operating medium-to-large in-memory engines, the 160 GB RAM pool enables consolidation without requiring higher core count tiers. However, applications bound by single-thread compute latency or requiring direct NVMe ephemeral storage must account for the lack of local scratch space and moderate single-core speeds.

The E20_v4 is tailored for relational database management systems, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, enterprise analytics backends, and JVM-based data processing pipelines that demand substantial memory buffers without excessive compute overhead.
description: Microsoft Azure E20_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual instance equipped with 20 vCPUs and 160 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor at 2.6 GHz. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features dedicated hardware threads, AVX-512 instructions with VNNI, and 35 MB of L3 cache, achieving an 8.0 GB per vCPU density. It contains no attached GPU accelerators and includes no local scratch disks, relying on remote block storage. Benchmarks place its multi-core compute and memory bandwidth in the standard midrange bracket, achieving 16.52 million Redis SET operations per second and steady multi-threaded compression metrics, despite modest single-threaded performance. The instance provides an efficient operational profile for enterprise workloads that prioritize memory volume over per-core clock frequency, such as in-memory caches, relational databases, analytics servers, and large-footprint application runtimes.
